content.text:
I've submitted **idx 14** (Bi 0.075, Cu 0.670, V 0.255) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.3e-7 A. With only 3 measurements across 142 compositions, I can't say whether it's actually the best in the library.

**How I chose:** at 2.06 eV (602 nm), BiVO₄ (band gap about 2.4 eV) should barely absorb light. So I aimed at the low-Bi, Cu-rich side, where copper vanadates have band gaps of about 1.9–2.0 eV.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.075 / 0.670 / 0.255 | 1.3e-7 A |
| 60 | 0.111 / 0.453 / 0.436 | 1.2e-7 A |
| 91 | 0.225 / 0.438 / 0.337 | 4e-8 A |

- **Low-Bi region:** idx 14 and idx 60 are close to each other, which suggests the low-Bi Cu-V edge performs about the same throughout rather than having one sharp peak.
- **More Bi:** idx 91 was about three times lower.
- **Bi-rich region:** I didn't measure it. I expected it to do poorly because BiVO₄ absorbs too little at this energy and CuBi₂O₄ is p-type, which suits a photocathode rather than a photoanode.

**Caveats:**
- **Model suggestion:** after the first two measurements, the model's top picks were all nearby low-Bi points, with high uncertainty. I tested the middle of the range instead, and that came out worst.
- **No XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD scans, so none of the phases above were confirmed.
- **Phase list:** the list of known phases was too large to return and I had no way to read the saved file, so I relied on what I already knew about these materials.
